adversarial_controls: A reserved call without a terminal receipt survives a simulated crash as indeterminate and is not retried.
A forged internally inconsistent terminal and a deeply nested unreadable terminal do not turn an indeterminate call into success.
Mutating visible stage inputs or work between calls, or exceeding the output inventory, blocks continuation.
A second session for one stage/run cannot reset the local tool-call or active-time budget; two concurrent inits leave one usable anchor.
A crash after a partial temporary anchor leaves no final anchor and permits a fresh init while the orphaned session remains unusable.
A call waits for anchor directory fsync after rename; EIO blocks it until a later successful fsync confirms durability.
A delay after reservation or during sandbox setup cannot launch the subprocess after the local UTC launch deadline.
A tool attempting to read a hidden reference received PermissionError and did not write the hidden-leaked marker.
known_scope_limit_control: Two separate stages copied from the same release and run_id each consumed one policy tool call with cap one. The local supervisor explicitly reports global_run_limits_enforced: false; a confirmatory global run needs an independent shared registry and custody.
